answer_1.quote: In this paper, our contributions are the following: (i) method and code for collecting long-input data for D2T (data-to-text) generation, along with a dataset of 537 long inputs; (ii) English and Irish system outputs for these 537 inputs, as well as human-written texts for a subset of 21 inputs; and...
datasets: New DBpedia-based dataset of 537 long-input triple sets (8-69 triples)
answer_1.outputs: Generated system outputs for 537 inputs in English and Irish; human-written texts for 21 inputs

answer_2.quote: ...we used several metrics proposed in to assess output diversity. For our analysis, we consider only the output texts used in the evaluation... We use the following four metrics as well as the average text length in words: (i) The N-Gram Diversity score considers n-grams of size 1 to 4 (NGD-1to4)... (ii) Self-Repetition (SelfRep-4)... (iii) Compression Rate (CompRate)... (iv) Chamfer Distance (ChamDist) ...

answer_3.quote: For assessing the quality of the different outputs, we ran and averaged the scores assigned by two different LLMs, GPT-o3 and Claudesonnet-3.7, two of the best models currently available. We used the same four dimensions as in WebNLG, text quality is assessed in its own right (Grammaticality and Fluency), and with respect to the input (No-omissions and No-additions), on a scale from 1 (lowest quality) to 7 (highest quality)...
methods: LLM-as-judge assessment with four dimensions on a 1-7 scale

answer_4.quote: Due to the cost and difficulty of performing an human evaluation on such a dataset, the texts are only assessed using an LLM-as-judge approach.
